Pretty good visual effects for the time.

In its defense, Pathecolor was NOT, as is sarcastically described here, color tinted black and white film. It was a major Eastmancolor-based process used in many films over the decades and often looked stunning. The color tinting in this film is simply because the original Russian movie was black and white and American distributors wanted a color release. Thus the Russian scenes were tinted, and the new footage was in color. The full-color sequences have just faded over time, as most Eastmancolor has.

I am glad I watched it. Lots of strange, bizarre science and movie making. Low budget for sure. No Oscar nominations here. But if your expectations are not too high, it is a charming unbelievable romp through the early years of what space travel was thought to include.

rv: Another Good Johnny Mack Brown Western Movie

The reviewer below sums up many of the main parts of the movie. It does, however, have a reasonable plot and acting for the typical western of the 1930's. Johnny Mack Brown does his usual good guy role. There are many horses racing from one place to another, which lengthens the movie time and in some cases adds to the suspense. This movie is not for everyone, but is good if the viewer likes old time westerns.
Johnny Mack Brown Sorts It All Out

Well, it seems some reviewers have problems with this movie - suspension of disbelief isn't possible, plot isn't believable - and where DID that Jewish peddler come from, what's he doing in this movie, what became of him, and who cares?
